title: Plans for three new homes among latest planning applications in Huntingdonshire
content: Plans for three new homes are among the latest planning applications across Huntingdonshire. Huntingdonshire District Council's notice covers planning applications as well as proposals affecting conservation areas and listed buildings. Representations should be made in writing within 14 days of the publication of the notice, which was published on November 18. To view the full public notice, go to https://publicnoticeportal.uk/notice/planning/6b0031b3918f0bd203637781. One application is listed under the notice's planning permission section. Application 26/02064/FUL seeks permission for three homes with detached garages, a shared private access drive, parking and landscaping on land to the rear of Meadow View, Warboys Road, Pidley. The following five applications are listed as affecting the setting of a conservation area. title: Plans go in for up to nine more homes on agricultural land on village outskirts
content: Plans have been submitted for up to nine homes on farmland behind eight approved houses in Warboys. The application seeks permission in principle for between six and nine homes on 0.85 hectares north of Heath Road, on the village’s north-eastern edge. If approved, the two schemes could provide up to 17 homes on this stretch of Heath Road. S Robinson submitted the latest proposal, with David Mead of The Planning Partnership as planning agent, and Huntingdonshire District Council granted permission for the eight-home development on October 20. A diagram showing the proposed layout of the development. (Image: HDC) Permission in principle would let the council decide whether the site, its residential use and the scale of development are acceptable. title: 5 Huntingdonshire planning applications that you should know about
content: Planning committees across Huntingdonshire are busy as ever, with plenty of applications and appeals coming through. We've compiled a list of just some of the applications that are currently pending or have been approved in our areas. Here are some that might have gone under the radar. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home."
